albums.title: Random Access Memories
albums.reason: With 2942 all-time plays, Daft Punk are your most-listened artist ever — and this swan song is lush, emotional, and probably hasn't had a full spin in a while.

albums.title: Hail to the Thief
albums.reason: Reckoner is your third most-played track of all time, so Radiohead clearly run deep — Hail to the Thief is the jagged, underappreciated one in the catalogue that rewards revisiting.

albums.title: Pocket Symphony
albums.reason: Air sit at over 1000 all-time plays and La femme d'argent and Sexy Boy are both deep in your history — Pocket Symphony is their quieter, more melancholic record that often gets overlooked.

albums.title: Hot Fuss
albums.reason: Mr. Brightside, A Dustland Fairytale, and All These Things That I've Done are all in your all-time top 50 tracks — going back to where it all started feels right.

albums.title: In Sides
albums.reason: Orbital clock 777 all-time plays for you and Don't Stop Me is a favourite — In Sides is their most ambitious, expansive record and a genuine classic of the era.

albums.title: Protection
albums.reason: Massive Attack have been with you for years across both your all-time and recent listening — Protection is their warmest, most soulful album and a perfect vault dive.

albums.title: The North Borders
albums.reason: Bonobo are in both your all-time and 12-month lists with 464 lifetime plays, and The North Borders sits in the sweet spot of that mid-2010s run before the more recent material you've been exploring.

albums.title: Moderat
albums.reason: Rusty Nails is in your all-time top 50 tracks and you've loved Moderat across multiple albums — their self-titled debut is the raw, restless one that started it all.

albums.title: The Trentemøller Chronicles
albums.reason: Trentemøller sits at 561 all-time plays and multiple albums are in your history — this double-disc compilation captures the peak of his early shadowy, hypnotic sound.

albums.title: Rounds
albums.reason: Four Tet showed up in your last 12 months with New Energy getting solid plays — Rounds is his most beloved earlier record and a key bridge between his IDM roots and the warmer direction you're clearly drawn to.

albums.title: The Devil's Walk
albums.reason: A Hum Of Maybe is your most-played Apparat album in the last year — The Devil's Walk is the darker, more cinematic record that preceded it and fills in a crucial part of the story.

albums.title: And They Have Escaped the Weight of Darkness
albums.reason: Ólafur Arnalds has been in your recent listening and Near Light is a previous pick you responded to — this earlier album is starker and more raw, hitting the same emotional vein.

albums.title: Galactic Melt
albums.reason: Your love of Daft Punk, Justice, and early-2010s electronic points straight here — Com Truise makes woozy, VHS-saturated synthwave that sits in exactly that late-night, analog-warm space.

albums.title: Every Day
albums.reason: Your all-time love of Massive Attack, Moby, and trip-hop adjacents makes this a natural fit — Cinematic Orchestra fuse live jazz, strings, and beats into something genuinely cinematic and emotionally weighty.

albums.title: Music Has the Right to Children
albums.reason: With Aphex Twin, Plaid, and Orbital all deep in your all-time listening, Boards of Canada are the missing piece — this debut is hazy, childhood-memory electronic music at its most affecting.

albums.title: Supermodified
albums.reason: Your taste runs deep into The Chemical Brothers, Orbital, and intricate electronic production — Amon Tobin's Supermodified chops jazz records into something futuristic and unlike almost anything else.

albums.title: Parades
albums.reason: Your love of Röyksopp's orchestral sweep and The Shins' melodic warmth points toward Efterklang — this Danish band made one of the most beautiful, choir-and-electronics records of the 2000s.

albums.title: Los Angeles
albums.reason: Your all-time passion for Aphex Twin, Plaid, and Modeselektor suggests you'd find a lot to love in Flying Lotus — this early record is beatmaking as psychedelic city portrait.

albums.title: The Return
albums.reason: Your recent deep dives into Oscar Peterson Trio, Portico Quartet, and Sault point clearly toward Kamaal Williams — his debut is a beautifully raw fusion of jazz, soul, and UK club energy.

albums.title: Black Focus
albums.reason: With Portico Quartet, St Germain, and jazz exploration running through your recent year, Black Focus — a one-album project of electric jazz and beats — feels like a direct next step.

albums.title: Persona
albums.reason: Your recent listening to Ben Lukas Boysen, Nils Frahm, and Hania Rani shows a love of precise, emotionally resonant electronic music — Rival Consoles' Persona hits that same nerve with more rhythmic urgency.

albums.title: Galaxy Garden
albums.reason: Your recent arc through Bibio, Four Tet, and O'Flynn's warm electronic textures leads naturally to Lone — Galaxy Garden is dizzyingly beautiful, beat-driven, and full of colour.

albums.title: Choose Your Weapon
albums.reason: Your recent listening to Sault, Charles Bradley, and Bill Withers shows a deep love of soul with substance — Hiatus Kaiyote's second album is funkier, stranger, and more ambitious than almost anything in the neo-soul space.

albums.title: Faking the Books
albums.reason: Your recent taste around Brambles, Hania Rani, and the quieter side of Khruangbin suggests you'd connect with Lali Puna's gentle, melancholic blend of indie pop and micro-electronics.

albums.title: We Will Always Love You
albums.reason: They're your most-played artist this month with 20 plays and No Bad Memories has been on heavy rotation — their third album is starrier and more spiritual than Wildflower, and a perfect companion to the listening you've been doing.

albums.title: Ambivalence Avenue
albums.reason: Bibio are your second most-played artist this month at 19 plays — Ambivalence Avenue is his warmest, most beloved record and a perfect pairing with the Answers and Ribbons listening you've been doing.

albums.title: Family Vacation
albums.reason: Axel Boman sits at 15 plays this month and Tell It To The Mountain has been a go-to — his debut album is even looser and sunnier, the perfect mood companion to where you are right now.

albums.title: Clark
albums.reason: Clark has appeared in both your last-month and last-7-days listening — this self-titled album is his most emotionally raw and varied, a great deeper cut from an artist clearly catching your attention.

albums.title: Resavoir
albums.reason: Resavoir showed up in your recent listening and Above the Clouds has been on rotation — their self-titled debut is where the whole joyful, ensemble jazz energy started, and it's worth hearing from the top.

albums.title: Crazy P Sound System
albums.reason: Crazy P are at 14 plays this month across two albums — this earlier compilation captures the raw, soulful house energy that makes them such a consistent presence in your current rotation.

songs.title: Voyager
songs.reason: Voyager sits at 87 plays in your all-time top tracks — it's one of their most emotionally pure moments and probably hasn't had a proper listen in years.

songs.title: Release the Pressure
songs.reason: Your fourth most-played track of all time at 120 plays — this one clearly meant something deep, and it deserves to come back around.

songs.title: Phantom Pt. II
songs.reason: Justice have 781 all-time plays and Phantom Pt. II sits at 83 plays in your top 50 — a track that hits like a freight train and probably takes you straight back to when you first heard it.

songs.title: Born Slippy
songs.reason: Born Slippy sits at 88 all-time plays in your top 50 — one of the most emotionally charged tracks in your listening history, and a true vault classic.

songs.title: Xtal
songs.reason: Xtal is at 73 plays in your all-time top 50 and Aphex Twin has 523 lifetime plays — this opener from Selected Ambient Works is gossamer, perfect, and deeply nostalgic.

songs.title: Hawkmoth
songs.reason: Hawkmoth sits at 82 plays in your all-time top 50 and Plaid have 512 lifetime plays — a gorgeous, intricate piece of IDM that clearly lodged itself deep in your musical memory.

songs.title: Midas Touch
songs.reason: Maribou State have 436 all-time plays and Beginner's Luck is in your top 50 — Midas Touch is from their more recent run and captures the warm, beat-led sound you clearly love from them.

songs.title: Kong
songs.reason: Bonobo are in both your all-time and recent listening history with hundreds of plays — Kong is a fan favourite from Black Sands that balances groove and atmosphere perfectly.

songs.title: Pyramid
songs.reason: Four Tet appeared in your last 12 months with New Energy getting dedicated listens — Pyramid is a peak moment from that era, radiant and endlessly repeatable.

songs.title: Reminder
songs.reason: You've loved multiple Moderat albums and Rusty Nails is in your all-time top 50 — Reminder is one of the most emotionally affecting tracks from their final record III.

songs.title: Rykketid
songs.reason: Trentemøller sits at 561 all-time plays and multiple albums deep in your history — Rykketid is a haunting, slow-burning gem from The Wait that shows his more cinematic, desolate side.

songs.title: Running to the Sea
songs.reason: Röyksopp are your fifth most-played all-time artist and The Inevitable End is in your history — Running to the Sea with Susanne Sundfør is one of the most beautiful things they've made.

songs.title: Brokendate
songs.reason: Your all-time love of Daft Punk's melodic side and Justice's electronic craftsmanship makes Com Truise a natural discovery — Brokendate is woozy, melancholic, and entirely its own world.

songs.title: Roygbiv
songs.reason: With Aphex Twin and Plaid both deep in your all-time listening, Boards of Canada are the gap worth filling — Roygbiv is their most beloved short piece, warm and bittersweet in equal measure.

songs.title: To Build a Home
songs.reason: Your deep love of Massive Attack, Moby, and emotionally resonant electronic music points straight to Cinematic Orchestra — To Build a Home is one of the great emotional peaks of that whole era.

songs.title: Do the Astral Plane
songs.reason: Your all-time love of Modeselektor, Aphex Twin, and inventive electronic production makes Flying Lotus a perfect discovery — Do the Astral Plane is playful, strange, and utterly compelling.

songs.title: Mirador
songs.reason: Your all-time passion for Röyksopp's orchestral sweep and The Avalanches' collage beauty leads naturally here — Mirador is big, choral, and emotionally overwhelming in the best way.

songs.title: Slowly
songs.reason: Your love of intricate electronic production across Plaid, Orbital, and The Chemical Brothers makes Amon Tobin a compelling discovery — Slowly is cinematic, restless, and unlike almost anything you've heard.

songs.title: Strings of Light
songs.reason: Your recent deep listening to Oscar Peterson Trio, Portico Quartet, and Sault suggests you're in a jazz-meets-electronic moment — Strings of Light is effortlessly cool and rhythmically alive.

songs.title: Wu Hen
songs.reason: Your recent arc through Portico Quartet, St Germain, and Sault points toward Kamaal Williams — Wu Hen is a slow-burning, deeply soulful piece that sits right in the pocket of your current sound.

songs.title: Airglow Fires
songs.reason: Your recent listening to Bibio, Four Tet, and O'Flynn's textured electronic sound leads naturally to Lone — Airglow Fires is radiant and immediately lovable.

songs.title: Breathing Underwater
songs.reason: Your recent love of Sault, Charles Bradley, and Khruangbin's warm-toned soul suggests Hiatus Kaiyote are a gap worth filling — Breathing Underwater is lush, complex, and deeply satisfying.

songs.title: Faking the Books
songs.reason: Your recent palette of Brambles, Hania Rani, and quieter Khruangbin moments points toward Lali Puna's soft, intimate blend of voice and electronics — this title track is a perfect entry point.

songs.title: The List
songs.reason: Your recent listening to Bill Withers, Dusty Springfield, and Sault shows a deep love of soulful, unhurried music — Moonchild's The List is exactly that, lush and late-night and warm.

songs.title: Because I'm Me
songs.reason: They're your most-played artist this month — Because I'm Me is one of their most joyful, soulful moments from Wildflower and fits perfectly with the energy you're in right now.

songs.title: Lovers' Carvings
songs.reason: Bibio are your second most-played artist this month — Lovers' Carvings is their most beloved track and given how deep you've been going into the catalogue, this deserves a fresh spin.

songs.title: Winter Linn
songs.reason: Clark has been in both your weekly and monthly listening — Winter Linn is a stunning, more tender moment from his self-titled album that shows the emotional range beneath the intensity.

songs.title: What Would I Do (Without Your Love)
songs.reason: Folamour appeared in your recent tracks list and in this month's listening — this track is a gorgeous slice of his soulful, emotionally rich house sound that fits your current mood perfectly.

songs.title: Weightless
songs.reason: Crazy P are at 14 plays this month and One True Light has been in your recent tracks — Weightless is a floating, blissful peak moment from their catalogue that matches where you are right now.

songs.title: All Night
songs.reason: Romare showed up in both your recent and monthly listening and Oblivion has been on rotation — All Night is a warm, groove-driven highlight from Love Songs: Part Two that fits this week's energy.
